title: Adaptive pin priority and telemetry-guided resolution for model onboarding
creator: Asha Kumar
description:
Problem: Customers pin model selection using tags, semver ranges, and commit hashes. Current resolver behavior is deterministic but lacks adaptive prioritization based on observed performance and rollout telemetry. This leads to noisier rollouts, higher cost during mismatched profiles, and brittle automatic fallbacks when a promoted model exhibits degraded latency or throughput for a given customer workload.

Goal: Implement an adaptive pin priority layer in the API/SDK resolver that: (1) preserves deterministic tie-breakers for tag/semver/hash resolution, (2) surface a telemetry-guided preference when multiple compatible identifiers exist (e.g., tag + semver range), and (3) exposes control knobs to customers to opt-in/out of telemetry-guided decisions. Provide clear SDK primitives and client-side telemetry to support runtime-aware model selection without surprising behavior for pinned configurations.
technical_design:
High-level approach: add a resolution priority vector to the server-side resolver and expose an opt-in client attribute 'adaptive_pin' that toggles telemetry-gated preference. Priority vector fields: explicit_hash > pinned_ref > semver_exact > semver_range > tag_latest, with an optional telemetry_bias that can bump candidates up or down based on observed p50/p95 latency, error rate, and token cost.

Server components: resolver module extension, telemetry scoring service (score executor), and safe-guarded fallback policy that enforces explicit hash stability.

Client SDK: expose ModelSelector object with fields: allow_adaptive_resolution (bool), bias_thresholds (latency_ms,error_rate_pct,cost_delta_pct), max_rollbacks (int). SDK will surface a deterministic log of resolution decisions for auditability.

Backward compatibility: default behavior remains current deterministic ordering unless allow_adaptive_resolution is true. Explicit commit-hash pins always win and will never be auto-swapped by telemetry adjustments.

Edge cases: cross-region model profile differences, transient infra-induced latency spikes, and customers who require strict release anchors. These are handled by region-scoped telemetry scores, cooldown windows, and opt-out flag respectively.
api_changes:
Add optional query parameter and JSON body fields to model resolution endpoints: 'adaptive_pin': boolean, 'telemetry_bias': string (one of 'latency','error','cost','composite'), 'bias_thresholds': object-encoded-as-string (json string). Add admin route to fetch resolution_decision_history for auditing per-request. Update model catalog GET to include 'performance_profiles' summary for regions.

API contract notes: if adaptive_pin is omitted -> legacy deterministic resolution. If provided -> server may reorder non-hash candidates using telemetry scores subject to configured constraints.
sdk_changes:
Add ModelSelector class to SDKs (Python/Node/Go) with methods: select_model(preferences, adaptive_pin=false, telemetry_bias=null, thresholds=null). SDK will record chosen_selector_trace and send minimal resolution telemetry (selector_id, chosen_ref, candidate_scores) to telemetry endpoint under the customer's org tag. Provide helper to set policy at client-level for all requests. Update SDK docs and add examples for opting in.

Degradation behavior: SDK will accept server-side decision and surface the chain-of-trust (why a model was chosen) to application logs for debugging.
migration_plan:
Phase 1 (opt-in): implement serverside resolver + SDK primitives; behind feature flag. Communicate to customers via release notes and samples.

Phase 2 (trial): invite internal tenants and 10 pilot customers to enable adaptive_pin and collect baseline telemetry for 2 weeks.

Phase 3 (wider availability): enable as GA opt-in and provide console toggle per-organization.

Phase 4 (future): consider opt-out flips for customers with at-scale benefits after opt-in success. Never auto-enable for customers with explicit commit-hash anchors.
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy resolver extension behind runtime feature flag. 2) Release SDK updates as minor versions (breaking? No). 3) Onboard pilot customers and monitor canaries (region and customer diversity). 4) Gradual ramp based on safety signals (latency, error rate, cost). 5) Provide console control and UI to view resolution decision history and score breakdowns.
metrics_and_telemetry:
Track these signals per-customer and per-region: resolution_count, adaptive_enabled_ratio, chosen_model_change_rate, selector_score_distribution, p50_latency_delta_vs_baseline, p95_latency_delta_vs_baseline, error_rate_delta, token_cost_delta, rollback_count. Emit resolution_decision event with fields: request_id, org_id, selector_id, candidates, scores, chosen_ref. Aggregated dashboards and alerts for >5% p95 degradation post-decision across pilot customers.

Privacy: ensure only aggregated scores and non-textual identifiers are stored; do not log prompt content.
test_plan:
Unit tests for resolver ordering matrix, property tests for stability (explicit hash never replaced), integration tests with synthetic telemetry to confirm score bumping and rollback flow, and e2e tests across SDK languages. Create canary job that simulates heavy KV-cache pressure and validates fallback to semver exact or explicit hash. Load tests to quantify cost changes under adaptive selection.

Acceptance criteria: deterministic fallback to explicit hash; telemetry scoring does not increase p95 above threshold in pilot customers; decision history accurately reconstructs choices.
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: noisy telemetry leading to oscillation between model candidates. Mitigation: implement cooldown windows, hysteresis, and conservative bias thresholds.

Risk: privacy/compliance concerns. Mitigation: strip textual payloads and limit telemetry retention; provide org-level opt-out.

Risk: customers misinterpret adaptive swaps as breaking changes. Mitigation: opt-in by default, clear docs, console audit trail, and email notifications for pilot participants.
acceptance_criteria: 1) SDKs expose model selector and customers can opt-in without breaking existing calls. 2) Resolver honors explicit commit hash pins under all conditions. 3) Pilot customers show no >5% increase in p95 latency or error rate after 2 weeks. 4) Decision history API returns consistent trace for 100% of resolution events in pilot. 5) Console UI shows per-org toggle and score breakdown.
